evidence.detail: `contains_cards_clause` uses a single `WHERE card IN (x,y,z) GROUP BY deck_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT card) = n` — for n>=3, MySQL must group all rows matching ANY of the n cards before filtering, causing timeout
`load_decks_by_cards` passes the result directly into `load_decks` with no query timeout or season filter
No merged PR found that addresses the archetype search timeout; the only related recent commit (20e3eed1) added card validation, not performance

triage.fix_sketch: Rewrite `contains_cards_clause` in `decksite/data/deck.py:522` so that for non-negated multi-card searches, instead of a single `GROUP BY … HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT card) = n`, it generates one `AND d.id IN (SELECT deck_id FROM deck_card WHERE card = {sqlescape(name)})` clause per card. Each per-card subquery uses the existing `idx_card_deck_id_sideboard_n` index efficiently, and the AND chain short-circuits without a large GROUP BY. ~15 lines changed, no schema migration.
triage.notes: The negated (NOT IN) path uses `>= 1` which is already a single-card-style check, so only the positive path needs the rewrite. Existing test coverage for `load_decks_by_cards` should be extended with a 3-card case.
